title: Signal Ensemble Calibration Labbook
content:
Purpose and context

This labbook captures exploratory work for creating an ensemble-style customer health score that combines heterogeneous adoption signals, product telemetry, and business-level indicators. Goal: produce a calibrated, monotonic score in [0,100] that maps to renewal probability buckets and drives triage routing and playbook automation.

Why an ensemble?
- Existing single-metric heuristics (MAU-based, last-activity) miss complementary failure modes.
- Ensemble lets us combine weak signals (feature usage, query latency, support interactions) and let a calibration layer correct scaling.
- We want interpretable per-signal contributions to aid playbook decisions.

Scope and constraints
- Use only data available in the last 90 days rolling window for near-term renewal predictions.
- Must run for all customers nightly at <30s latency on the scoring pipeline.
- Score will be surfaced in the CS dashboard and used to drive automated risk flags and recommended actions.

Input signal catalogue (initial list)
- product_active_days_30: number of days with >=1 API request in last 30d (0-30)
- avg_lat_per_request_30: median request latency (ms) over 30d (lower is better)
- embed_qps_95: 95th percentile QPS for embeddings on peak day (normalized by reserved capacity)
- model_rollouts_count: number of versions used in prod rollout (higher may indicate churn)
- eval_regressions: count of recent quality regressions detected against benchmark prompts (0,1,2+)
- support_tickets_90: number of critical support tickets in 90d
- console_logins_30: number of unique console agent logins by customer admins
- cache_hit_rate: KV/prefix cache hit rate (0-1)
- docs_interactions: count of in-product doc/knowledge-base lookups (proxy for exploration)

Preprocessing steps (working notes)
1) Winsorize extreme tails at 1st/99th percentiles for continuous signals.
2) Transformations: log(x+1) for counts with heavy tails; negative-log for latency to align directionality.
3) Missingness: treat missing as signal-specific default (e.g., null cache_hit_rate -> 0.1), but flag via separate binary missing_* features for calibration analysis.

Ensemble architecture (high level)
- Stage A: per-signal normalization -> continuous standardized scores in [-3,3]. Use robust scaler (median, IQR).
- Stage B: Light-weight scoring model (two options to evaluate):
    Option 1: Logistic regression with L2 penalty -> outputs probability p in [0,1].
    Option 2: Gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost) returning raw probability, then isotonic calibration.
- Stage C: Monotonic transform to 0-100 and bucketing logic: score100 = round(p * 100).
- Stage D: Explainability layer: SHAP-lite (per-signal additive contributions summed to p) and top-3 contributing signals attached to record.

Calibration heuristics and thresholds (first pass)
- Risk tier mapping derived from historical renewal outcomes (12-month labels):
    - Tier A (Urgent): score100 <= 25 -> immediate CS outreach and high-touch expansion review
    - Tier B (At-risk): 26-50 -> playbook with technical review and product health audit
    - Tier C (Watch): 51-75 -> automated nudges and monitor for regression
    - Tier D (Healthy): 76-100 -> standard renewals cadence
- Risk flags:
    - Immediate-risk-flag if support_tickets_90 >= 2 AND model_regressions >= 1
    - Latency-risk-flag if avg_lat_per_request_30 above baseline 2x AND embed_qps_95 drops below capacity threshold
    - Engagement-drop-flag if product_active_days_30 decreases by >40% vs prior 30d window

Labeling methodology (where training labels come from)
- Positive label: customer renewed in the following 90d window (binary). Use rolling windows to increase sample size.
- Negative label: churned/contract not renewed or reduced committed capacity by >50% within 90d.
- Censoring: exclude customers that were acquired or restructured (flagged via CRM).

Calibration experiments (planned)
1) Baseline logistic regression with equalized class weights; cross-validated AUC, Brier score.
2) Isotonic regression on top of XGBoost to force monotonic probabilities. Compare reliability diagrams.
3) Calibrate per-customer-tier: separate models for SMB vs Enterprise vs Strategic to handle scale effects.
4) Feature ablation study to find minimal feature set that preserves AUC within 2 points.
5) Time-decay experiments: weighted training with recency half-life of 60d vs uniform.

Early empirical notes (pilot run on last 18 months)
- Logistic baseline AUC: 0.71; XGBoost AUC: 0.76 on hold-out; uncalibrated probabilities were overconfident (Brier ~0.18).
- Isotonic calibration reduced Brier to 0.12 and tightened reliability curve notably for p in [0.1,0.4].
- Top 3 SHAP signals (by average absolute contribution): product_active_days_30, cache_hit_rate, support_tickets_90.
- Notable segment behavior: customers with high console_logins_30 but low product_active_days_30 often indicate admin-only access; these should be deprioritized for expansion playbooks.

Action mapping prototype (how CS should act based on score + flags)
- score100 <= 25 OR Immediate-risk-flag -> "Emergency" process: 24-hour response SLA, technical deep-dive SRE + Solutions Eng, proposed temporary quota increase or hotfix path.
- 26-50 AND support_tickets_90 >= 1 -> "Technical Rehab" playbook: schedule health check, run prompt-level evals, recommend configuration/quantization to reduce cost.
- 51-75 -> "Nudge" playbook: curated content + in-console guided checklist, invite to webinars.
- 76-100 -> "Expansion" playbook: surface new features, recommend pilot templates with success metrics.

Monitoring and drift detection
- Nightly scoring logs -> compute score distribution KS test vs training baseline; alert on two-sigma shifts in median.
- Per-signal drift: track population percentiles (10/50/90) and alert on >30% relative change.
- Model fairness check: ensure that model does not systematically underpredict for specific verticals (telecom, finance) — run per-vertical lift reports monthly.

Operational checklist for rollout (MVP)
- Build nightly batch job: feature extraction + scoring + explainability snapshot (top 3 signals).
- Backfill 18 months to populate historical buckets for dashboard.
- Add webhooks for urgent-tier customers to trigger PagerDuty and CS Slack channel.
- Create CS training one-pager and playbook runbooks for each risk flag.

Open questions and next steps (research backlog)
- Should we force monotonicity for specific signals (e.g., product_active_days_30 must always increase score)? explore monotonic GBMs.
- How to encode product launches or seasonal campaigns that inflate activity but don’t reflect health? create campaign tag features.
- Can we build a synthetic counterfactual to estimate "would-have-renewed" probability for customers with contract modifications?
- Run a 6-week A/B with CS teams: auto-assigned playbooks vs manual triage to measure time-to-resolution and renewal deltas.

Appendix: sample scoring pseudo-code
1) raw = extract_signals(customer_id, window=90)
2) pre = winsorize_and_transform(raw)
3) z = robust_standardize(pre, medians, iqr)
4) p_raw = model.predict_proba(z)
5) p_cal = isotonic_calibrator.transform(p_raw)
6) score100 = int(round(p_cal * 100))

Note: keep this document as the single-source-of-truth for the experimental design. I'll update with experiment results, plots, and exported calibration curves in subsequent revisions.

-- Asha

(Notes to self: ask Solutions Eng to validate that cache_hit_rate is correctly computed across dedicated vs hosted customers — metric semantics differ for private deployments.)
